title.zh: 卷六十五 志第十八 五行三
title.raw: 卷六十五 志第十八 五行三 Volume 65 Treatises 18: Five Elements 3

sentences.zh: 文章還沒有進行過校對和格式化，或文章還不全，不能保證任何部分可靠。

translations.literal: The article has not yet undergone proofreading and formatting, or the article is still incomplete; no part can be guaranteed reliable.
translations.idiomatic: This text has not been proofread or fully formatted, and portions may still be missing; nothing in it should be treated as authoritative.

sentences.zh: 曲直，木之性也。

translations.literal: Crookedness and straightness are the nature of wood.
translations.idiomatic: To bend and to stand straight belong to the nature of wood.

sentences.zh: 木失其性，则为妖祥。

translations.literal: When wood loses its nature, then there are strange omens and portents.
translations.idiomatic: When wood departs from its proper nature, it manifests as uncanny signs—whether ill or auspicious.

sentences.zh: 旧说以狂咎、木冰、恒雨、服妖、龟孽、鸡祸、青眚、青祥之类，皆属之木，今从之。

translations.literal: Older theories hold that mad culprits, tree-ice, constant rain, garment anomalies, turtle calamities, chicken portents, green blight, green auspices, and the like all belong to wood; this treatise now follows that classification.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier cosmologists grouped phenomena such as violent madness, glazed trees, unending rain, anomalous dress, turtle afflictions, cock omens, green pestilence, and green felicities under the Wood phase; this chapter adopts that tradition.

sentences.zh: 太平兴国六年正月，瑞安县民张度解木五片，皆有“天下太平”字。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo, the commoner Zhang Du of Ruian County split five pieces of wood, each bearing the characters "Under Heaven at Peace."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Taiping Xingguo 6 (981), Zhang Du, a man of Ruian County, cleaved five planks of timber, and every piece showed the inscription "All under Heaven is at peace."

sentences.zh: 至道六年，修昭应宫，有木断之，文如点漆，贯彻上下，体若梵书。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhidao, while repairing Zhaoying Palace, a piece of wood was cut; its markings were like dots of lacquer, running through it top to bottom, in form like Brahmi script.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 6 (1000), during repairs to Zhaoying Palace, workers split a timber whose grain appeared as jet-black lacquer tracery running the full length of the log, shaped like Indic script.

sentences.zh: 十一月，襄州民刘士家生木。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, wood grew at the home of the commoner Liu Shi in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, timber sprouted inside the house of Liu Shi, a man of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有文如龙、鱼、凤、鹤之状。

translations.literal: It bore markings in the shapes of dragons, fish, phoenixes, and cranes.
translations.idiomatic: The grain formed patterns resembling dragons, fish, phoenixes, and cranes.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，抚州修天庆观，解木有文如墨画云气、峰峦、人物、衣冠之状。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, while repairing Tianqing Abbey in Fuzhou, split wood bore markings like ink paintings of clouds, peaks, human figures, and caps and robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year (1001), as Tianqing Abbey in Fuzhou was being restored, a log that was split open showed markings like ink-wash clouds, mountain ranges, figures, and court dress.

sentences.zh: 七月，彰明县崇仙观柱有文为道士形及北斗七星象。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, a pillar at Chongxian Abbey in Zhangming County bore markings in the form of a Daoist priest and the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, a column at Chongxian Abbey in Zhangming County displayed grain patterns shaped like a Daoist adept and the Big Dipper.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符八年，晋州庆唐观古柏中别生槐，长丈余。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, from an ancient cypress at Qingtang Abbey in Jin Prefecture a separate locust tree grew, more than a zhang in height.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 8 (1015), a locust tree more than ten feet tall sprouted from within an ancient cypress at Qingtang Abbey in Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天圣元年二月，河阳柳二本连理。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Tiansheng, two willow trees at Heyang grew as one interlaced trunk.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tiansheng 1 (1023), two willows at Heyang fused into a single intergrown trunk.

sentences.zh: 六月，河阳甗、枣各连理。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, at Heyang the earthenware jar tree and the jujube each grew as interlaced trunks.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, both the jar tree and the jujube at Heyang produced conjoined trunks.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，绵谷县松柏同本异干。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, in Miangu County pine and cypress shared one root but had separate trunks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year (1027), in Miangu County a pine and a cypress rose from a single root with two distinct trunks.

sentences.zh: 九年十月，公井县冬青木连理。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the ninth year, the holly at Gongjing County grew as an interlaced trunk.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the ninth year (1031), a holly at Gongjing County formed a conjoined trunk.

sentences.zh: 明道元年八月，黄州橘木及柿木连枝。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Mingdao, at Huang Prefecture orange wood and persimmon wood joined branches.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Mingdao 1 (1032), an orange tree and a persimmon at Huang Prefecture shared interlocking branches.

sentences.zh: 康定元年十月，始兴县柑两本连理。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Kangding, two tangerine trees at Shixing County grew as one interlaced trunk.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kangding 1 (1040), two tangerine trees at Shixing County fused into a single intergrown trunk.

sentences.zh: 庆历三年十二月，澧州献瑞木，有文曰“太平之道”。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Qingli, Li Prefecture presented an auspicious tree bearing the inscription "The Way of Great Peace."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Qingli 3 (1043), Li Prefecture offered up a felicitous timber inscribed with the words "The path to universal peace."

sentences.zh: 六年九月甲辰，登州有巨木浮海而出者三千余。

translations.literal: On the jiachen day of the ninth month of the sixth year, at Deng Prefecture more than three thousand huge timbers floated out of the sea.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the ninth month in the sixth year (1046), more than three thousand enormous logs drifted ashore at Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 治平四年六月，汀州进桐木板二，有文曰“天下太平”。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Zhiping, Ting Prefecture presented two paulownia planks bearing the inscription "Under Heaven at Peace."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhiping 4 (1067), Ting Prefecture submitted two paulownia boards marked with the characters "All under Heaven is at peace."

sentences.zh: 熙宁元年三月，简州木连理。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Xining, trees at Jian Prefecture grew as interlaced trunks.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Xining 1 (1068), trees at Jian Prefecture formed conjoined trunks.

sentences.zh: 是岁，英州因雷震，一山梓树尽枯而为龙脑，价为之贱，至京师，一两才值钱一千四百。

translations.literal: That year, at Ying Prefecture because of thunder, all the catalpa trees on one mountain withered and turned into borneol; the price therefore fell, and when it reached the capital, one liang was worth only fourteen hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, lightning struck Ying Prefecture and every catalpa on one mountain withered into crude borneol, flooding the market; by the time it reached the capital, a single tael fetched only 1,400 cash.

sentences.zh: 二年，建州民杨纬言：“元年三月，大雷雨，所居之西有黄龙见，下获一木如龙，而形未具。

translations.literal: In the second year, the commoner Yang Wei of Jian Prefecture said: "In the third month of the first year, in a great thunderstorm, to the west of my dwelling a yellow dragon appeared; below I obtained a piece of wood like a dragon, but its form was not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1069), Yang Wei of Jian Prefecture reported: "In the third month of the first year, during a violent thunderstorm, a yellow dragon appeared west of my home. I found beneath it a log shaped like a dragon, though its form was still incomplete.

sentences.zh: 七月，大雷雨，复有龙飞其下。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, in a great thunderstorm, again a dragon flew beneath it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month another thunderstorm came, and again a dragon was seen flying below.

sentences.zh: 及霁，木龙尾、翼、足皆具，归合旧木，宛然一体。”

translations.literal: When the sky cleared, the wooden dragon's tail, wings, and feet were all complete; reunited with the old wood, it was plainly one whole."
translations.idiomatic: When the storm cleared, the log now had tail, wings, and feet fully formed; fitted back to the original piece, the two formed a seamless whole."

sentences.zh: 图象以进。

translations.literal: A diagram was made and presented.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a painted record of the phenomenon to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十年八月乙巳，惠州柚木有文曰“王帝万年，天下太平”。

translations.literal: On the yisi day of the eighth month of the tenth year, a pomelo tree at Huizhou bore the inscription "The king and emperor for ten thousand years; under Heaven at peace."
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the eighth month in the tenth year (1077), a pomelo at Huizhou displayed the inscription "May the Son of Heaven reign ten thousand years; all under Heaven at peace."

sentences.zh: 元丰元年五月，剑州木连理。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yuanfeng, trees at Jian Prefecture grew as interlaced trunks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Yuanfeng (1078), trees at Jian Prefecture formed conjoined trunks.

sentences.zh: 三年六月己未，饶州长山雨木子数亩，状类山芋子，味香而辛，土人以为桂子，又曰“菩提子”，明道中尝有之。

translations.literal: On the jiwei day of the sixth month of the third year, at Changshan in Rao Prefecture wooden seeds rained over several mu; they resembled taro seeds, fragrant and pungent; locals took them for cassia seeds, also called "bodhi seeds"; this had occurred once in the Mingdao era.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day of the sixth month in the third year (1080), tree seeds fell over several acres at Changshan in Rao Prefecture. They looked like taro seeds, smelled sweet yet tasted sharp, and locals called them cassia seeds or "bodhi seeds"—a phenomenon that had appeared once before in the Mingdao period.

sentences.zh: 是岁大稔。

translations.literal: That year there was a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought an abundant harvest.

sentences.zh: 十二月，泌阳县甘棠木连理。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the flowering quince at Biyang County grew as an interlaced trunk.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, a flowering quince at Biyang County formed a conjoined trunk.

sentences.zh: 六年五月，卫真县洞霄宫枯槐生枝叶。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year, the withered locust at Dongxiao Palace in Weizhen County put forth branches and leaves.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year (1083), a dead locust at Dongxiao Palace in Weizhen County sprouted fresh branches and leaves.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年八月己丑，杭州民俞举庆七世同居，家园木连理。

translations.literal: On the jichou day of the eighth month of the first year of Yuanyou, the commoner Yu Juqing of Hangzhou celebrated seven generations dwelling together; trees in his household garden grew as interlaced trunks.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day of the eighth month of Yuanyou 1 (1086), Yu Juqing of Hangzhou, whose family had lived together for seven generations, found the trees in his garden fused into conjoined trunks.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，德州木连理。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, trees at De Prefecture grew as interlaced trunks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year (1090), trees at De Prefecture formed conjoined trunks.

sentences.zh: 元符元年八月，施州李木连理。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yuanfu, plum trees at Shi Prefecture grew as interlaced trunks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yuanfu 1 (1098), plum trees at Shi Prefecture formed conjoined trunks.

sentences.zh: 二年九月，眉山县桤木二株，异根同干，木枝相附。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year, two alder trees at Meishan County had separate roots but one trunk, their branches adhering to each other.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year (1099), two alders at Meishan County shared a single trunk from distinct roots, their branches intertwined.

sentences.zh: 崇宁四年正月，襄城县李、梨木连理。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Chongning, at Xiangcheng County plum and pear trees grew as interlaced trunks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chongning 4 (1105), plum and pear trees at Xiangcheng County produced conjoined trunks.

sentences.zh: 大观元年三月，湟州栏木生叶。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Daguan, fence wood at Huang Prefecture produced leaves.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Daguan 1 (1107), a fence post at Huang Prefecture sprouted leaves.

sentences.zh: 八月，瑞州、永兴军并木连理。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Rui Prefecture and Yongxing Circuit both had trees growing as interlaced trunks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, both Rui Prefecture and Yongxing Circuit reported conjoined trunks.

sentences.zh: 二年十二月，岢岚军园池生瑞木。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year, the garden pool at Kelan Army produced an auspicious tree.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year (1108), a felicitous tree appeared in the garden pond at Kelan Army.

sentences.zh: 政和三年七月，玉华殿万年枝木连理。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Zhenghe, the evergreen branch tree at Yuhua Hall grew as an interlaced trunk.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhenghe 3 (1113), the evergreen ceremonial branch at Yuhua Hall formed a conjoined trunk.

sentences.zh: 南雄州枫木连理。

translations.literal: At Nanxiong Prefecture maple trees grew as interlaced trunks.
translations.idiomatic: Maples at Nanxiong Prefecture also produced conjoined trunks.

sentences.zh: 十月，武义县木根有“万宋年岁”四字。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, a tree root at Wuyi County bore the four characters "Ten Thousand Years of the Song."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, a tree root at Wuyi County displayed the four characters "Ten thousand years of Song."

sentences.zh: 四年，建州木连理。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, trees at Jian Prefecture grew as interlaced trunks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1114), trees at Jian Prefecture formed conjoined trunks.

sentences.zh: 六月，沅陵县江涨，流出楠木二十七，可为明堂梁柱，蔡京等拜表贺。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the river at Yuanling County rose and washed out twenty-seven nanmu timbers fit for pillars and beams of the Bright Hall; Cai Jing and others submitted congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, floodwaters at Yuanling County cast up twenty-seven nanmu logs suitable for Bright Hall pillars; Cai Jing and his colleagues memorialized the throne with congratulations.

sentences.zh: 九月丙申，彭城县柏开华。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day of the ninth month, cypress at Pengcheng County blossomed.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day of the ninth month, a cypress at Pengcheng County burst into flower.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛丑，元氏县民王寘屋柱槐木再生枝叶，高四十余尺。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day of the twelfth month, the locust pillar of Wang Zhi's house at Yuanshi County put forth branches and leaves anew, more than forty chi high.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the twelfth month, the locust support beam in Wang Zhi's house at Yuanshi County sprouted new branches and leaves standing more than forty feet tall.

sentences.zh: 是岁，邵州海棠木连理，泽州、台州槐木连理，荆门军紫薇木连理。

translations.literal: That year, crabapple at Shao Prefecture, locust at Ze and Tai Prefectures, and crape myrtle at Jingmen Army all grew as interlaced trunks.
translations.idiomatic: That year conjoined trunks appeared among crabapples at Shao Prefecture, locusts at Ze and Tai Prefectures, and crape myrtle at Jingmen Army.

sentences.zh: 六年，坊、兖、洪、明、夔、徐、新、全、隰、太平州并木连理。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Fang, Yan, Hong, Ming, Kui, Xu, Xin, Quan, Xi, and Taiping Prefectures all had trees growing as interlaced trunks.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1116), Fang, Yan, Hong, Ming, Kui, Xu, Xin, Quan, Xi, and Taiping Prefectures all reported conjoined trunks.

sentences.zh: 梅州枯木生枝。

translations.literal: At Mei Prefecture withered wood put forth branches.
translations.idiomatic: At Mei Prefecture dead timber sprouted new branches.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年四月，永州民刘思析薪，有“天下太平”字。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Xuanhe, the commoner Liu Si of Yong Prefecture split firewood bearing the characters "Under Heaven at Peace."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xuanhe 2 (1120), Liu Si of Yong Prefecture, splitting firewood, found the inscription "All under Heaven is at peace."

sentences.zh: 绍兴十四年四月，虔州民毁欹屋析柱，木里有文曰：“天下太平”，时守臣薛弼上之，方大乱，近木妖也。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year of Shaoxing, a commoner of Qian Prefecture demolished a leaning house and split a pillar; inside the wood was the inscription "Under Heaven at Peace"; the prefectural defender Xue Bi presented it—just as great disorder had begun; this was a wood omen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Shaoxing 14 (1144), a man of Qian Prefecture tore down a tilting house and split a pillar, finding within the grain the words "All under Heaven is at peace." Prefect Xue Bi forwarded it to court even as the realm was sliding into chaos—a clear case of wood working as an uncanny portent.

sentences.zh: 二十年八月，福州冲虚观皂荚木翠叶再实。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twentieth year, the honeylocust at Chongxu Abbey in Fuzhou, with emerald leaves, bore fruit a second time.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twentieth year (1150), the honeylocust at Chongxu Abbey in Fuzhou, its leaves still green, fruited a second time in one season.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，建德县定林寺桑生李实，栗生桃实，占曰：“木生异实，国主殃。”

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, at Dinglin Temple in Jiande County mulberry bore plum fruit and chestnut bore peach fruit; prognostication says: "When wood bears strange fruit, the ruler suffers calamity."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1151), at Dinglin Temple in Jiande County, mulberry trees bore plums and chestnuts bore peaches. The omen books say: "When trees yield alien fruit, the sovereign meets disaster."

sentences.zh: 二十五年十月，赣州献太平木。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-fifth year, Gan Prefecture presented Peace Timber.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twenty-fifth year (1155), Gan Prefecture offered up a "timber of peace."

sentences.zh: 时秦桧擅朝，喜饰太平，郡国多上草木之妖以为瑞。

translations.literal: At that time Qin Hui monopolized the court, delighted to adorn an age of peace; commanderies and states often presented plant anomalies as auspicious signs.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui then dominated the court and loved to parade an era of peace; prefectures and circuits flooded the capital with botanical oddities dressed up as felicitations.

sentences.zh: 绍兴间，汉阳 军有插榴枝于石罅，秀茂成阴，岁有花实者。

translations.literal: During the Shaoxing era, at Hanyang Army someone planted a pomegranate branch in a stone crevice; it flourished into shade and bore flowers and fruit every year.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoxing period at Hanyang Circuit, someone wedged a pomegranate cutting into a crack in stone; it grew lush shade and flowered and fruited year after year.

sentences.zh: 初，郡狱有诬服孝妇杀姑，妇不能自明，属行刑者插髻上华于石隙，曰：“生则可以验吾冤。”

translations.literal: Initially, in the prefectural prison a filial daughter-in-law had falsely confessed to killing her mother-in-law; the woman could not clear herself and charged the executioner to plant the flower from her hairpin in a stone crevice, saying: "If it lives, my innocence can be proved."
translations.idiomatic: The story began in the prefectural jail, where a dutiful daughter-in-law had been forced to confess to murdering her mother-in-law though she could not prove her innocence. She asked the executioner to plant the blossom from her hairpin in a stone crack, saying, "If it lives, you will know I was wronged."

sentences.zh: 行刑者如其言，后果生。

translations.literal: The executioner did as she said, and afterward it indeed lived.
translations.idiomatic: The executioner did as she asked, and the cutting later flourished.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十六年三月，扬州桑生瓜，樱桃生茄，此草木互为妖也。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixteenth year of Chunxi, at Yangzhou mulberry bore melons and cherry bore eggplant; these were plants mutually becoming omens.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Chunxi 16 (1189), at Yangzhou mulberry trees bore melons and cherries bore eggplants—plants crossing nature to become each other's portents.

sentences.zh: 七月，晋陵县民析薪，中有木字曰“绍熙五年”，如是者二。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, a commoner of Jinling County split firewood; within the wood were the characters "Shaoxi fifth year"—two such cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, a man of Jinling County splitting firewood found the grain marked "Shaoxi year five"—and this happened twice.

sentences.zh: 是时，绍熙犹未改元，其后果止五年，此近木妖也。

translations.literal: At that time Shaoxi had not yet been proclaimed as an era name; afterward the reign indeed lasted only five years; this was a wood omen.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxi had not yet been proclaimed when the signs appeared; the reign in fact ended after only five years—a near-perfect wood portent.

sentences.zh: 绍熙四年，富阳县栗生来禽实。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxi, chestnut at Fuyang County bore cherry fruit.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi 4 (1193), chestnuts at Fuyang County bore cherry-like fruit.

sentences.zh: 五年，行都雨木，与《唐志》贞元陈留雨木同占，木生于下而自上陨者，将有上下易位之象。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the mobile capital had a rain of wood; the same prognostication as Chenliu in Zhenyuan in the Tang Treatises—wood born below yet falling from above—signifies that high and low will exchange positions.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1194), the temporary capital experienced a rain of wood. The Tang History records the same omen at Chenliu in Zhenyuan 1 (785): when what grows below falls from above, ruler and ruled are about to trade places.

sentences.zh: 嘉定六年五月己巳，严州淳安、遂安、桐庐三县大木自拔，占曰：“木自拔，国将乱。”

translations.literal: On the jisi day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Jiading, in Chun'an, Suian, and Tonglu counties of Yan Prefecture great trees uprooted themselves; prognostication says: "When wood uproots itself, the state will fall into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day of the fifth month in Jiading 6 (1213), great trees in Chun'an, Suian, and Tonglu under Yan Prefecture tore themselves from the ground. The omen books read: "When trees uproot themselves, the realm is heading for chaos."

sentences.zh: 景定四年五月，成都太祖庙侧大木仆，忽起立，生三芽。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Jingding, a great tree beside the Taizu Temple in Chengdu fell, then suddenly stood up again and produced three shoots.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Jingding 4 (1263), a great tree beside the Taizu Temple in Chengdu toppled, then abruptly righted itself and put forth three sprouts.

sentences.zh: 德祐二年正月戊辰，宝应县民析薪，中有“天太下赵”四字，献之，制置使李庭芝尝以钱五千。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day of the first month of the second year of Deyou, a commoner of Baoying County split firewood bearing the four characters "Heaven above, Zhao below"; he presented it, and the commissioner Li Tingzhi once rewarded him with five thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the first month in Deyou 2 (1276), a man of Baoying County splitting firewood found the four characters rearranged to read "Heaven above, Zhao below"—a cryptic prophecy of the dynasty's fall. He presented the log, and Commissioner Li Tingzhi once gave him five thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 咸平六年十一月庚戌，雨木冰。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day of the eleventh month of the sixth year of Xianping, tree-ice rained.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day of the eleventh month in Xianping 6 (1003), glazed ice formed on trees.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年正月戊寅，京师雨木冰。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day of the first month of the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the capital had tree-ice rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day of the first month in Dazhong Xiangfu 5 (1012), the capital saw trees encased in ice.

sentences.zh: 天禧五年正月戊寅，京师雨木冰。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day of the first month of the fifth year of Tianxi, the capital had tree-ice rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day of the first month in Tianxi 5 (1021), the capital again saw glazed tree-ice.

sentences.zh: 庆历三年十二月丁巳，雪木冰，占曰：“兵象也。”

translations.literal: On the dingsi day of the twelfth month of the third year of Qingli, snow froze on trees as ice; prognostication says: "This is a sign of war."
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day of the twelfth month in Qingli 3 (1043), snow left trees encased in ice. The omen books read: "This presages war."

sentences.zh: 嘉祐元年正月，雨木冰。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Jiayou, tree-ice rained.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jiayou 1 (1056), trees were glazed with ice.

sentences.zh: 治平二年十月乙巳，雨木冰。

translations.literal: On the yisi day of the tenth month of the second year of Zhiping, tree-ice rained.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the tenth month in Zhiping 2 (1065), tree-ice formed.

sentences.zh: 熙宁三年十月、八年正月、九年正月，京师雨木冰。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Xining, and the first months of the eighth and ninth years, the capital had tree-ice rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Xining 3 (1070) and the first months of Xining 8 and 9, the capital saw glazed tree-ice.

sentences.zh: 元祐八年二月，京师大寒，霰、雪，雨木冰。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year of Yuanyou, the capital had severe cold, graupel and snow, and tree-ice rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yuanyou 8 (1093), bitter cold, graupel, and snow left the capital's trees encased in ice.

sentences.zh: 宣和五年十月乙酉，雨木冰。

translations.literal: On the yiyou day of the tenth month of the fifth year of Xuanhe, tree-ice rained.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the tenth month in Xuanhe 5 (1123), tree-ice formed.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年十月乙卯，雨木冰。

translations.literal: On the yimao day of the tenth month of the first year of Jingkang, tree-ice rained.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day of the tenth month in Jingkang 1 (1126), tree-ice formed.

sentences.zh: 二年正月丁酉，雨木冰。

translations.literal: On the dingyou day of the first month of the second year, tree-ice rained.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the first month in the second year (1127), tree-ice formed again.

sentences.zh: 绍熙五年十一月辛亥，雨木冰。

translations.literal: On the xinhai day of the eleventh month of the fifth year of Shaoxi, tree-ice rained.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day of the eleventh month in Shaoxi 5 (1194), tree-ice formed.

sentences.zh: 宣和六年，御楼观灯，时开封尹设次以弹压于西观下，帝从六宫于其上，以观天府之断决者，帘幕深密，下无由知。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuanhe, at the Imperial Tower lantern viewing, the Kaifeng intendant set up a station to suppress disorder below the west viewing stand; the emperor followed the six palaces above to watch the Celestial Treasury's judgments; curtains were deep and dense, and those below had no way to know.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 6 (1124), during the lantern festival at the Imperial Tower, the Kaifeng prefect posted guards below the west gallery to keep order while the emperor, accompanied by the consorts, watched legal judgments from the Celestial Treasury chamber above. Heavy curtains hid everything from the crowd below.

sentences.zh: 众中忽有人跃出，黑色布衣，若寺僧童行状，以手画帘，出指斥语。

translations.literal: Suddenly from the crowd someone leaped out, in black plain cloth like a temple acolyte, drew his hand across the curtain, and uttered words of rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a figure burst from the crowd—dressed in plain black like a temple novice—swept his hand across the curtain and shouted accusations.

sentences.zh: 执于观下，帝怒甚，令中使传旨治之。

translations.literal: He was seized below the viewing stand; the emperor was greatly angered and ordered a palace envoy to convey an edict to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Guards seized him at the foot of the gallery. The emperor, furious, sent a palace eunuch with orders to punish him severely.

sentences.zh: 箠掠乱下，又加炮烙，询其谁何，略不一语，亦无痛楚之状。

translations.literal: Blows from cudgels rained down chaotically, then branding was added; asked who he was, he scarcely spoke a word and showed no sign of pain.
translations.idiomatic: They beat him with clubs, then applied hot irons, yet he barely spoke when questioned and showed no sign of suffering.

sentences.zh: 又断其足筋，俄施刀脔，血肉狼籍。

translations.literal: They also severed the tendons of his feet; soon knives dismembered him, flesh and blood strewn everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: They severed the tendons in his legs, then hacked him apart until flesh and blood littered the ground.

sentences.zh: 帝大不 悦，为罢一夕之欢，竟不得其何人，付狱尽之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly displeased, ended the night's festivities for this, and never learned who he was; he was handed to the prison and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply unsettled, the emperor cut the night's revelry short. His identity was never discovered; he was thrown into prison and killed.

sentences.zh: 七年八月，都城东门外鬻菜夫至宣德门下，忽若迷罔，释荷担向门戟手，出悖骂语。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year, a vegetable peddler at the capital's east gate reached Xuande Gate, suddenly as if dazed, set down his carrying pole, faced the gate with folded arms, and uttered words of reckless abuse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the seventh year (1125), a vegetable seller from outside the east gate reached Xuande Gate, fell into a trance, set down his load, faced the gate with folded arms, and hurled wild curses.

sentences.zh: 且曰：“太祖皇帝、神宗皇帝使 我来道，尚宜速改也。”

translations.literal: He also said: "Taizu Emperor and Shenzong Emperor sent me to announce: you should still reform quickly."
translations.idiomatic: He cried, "Taizu and Shenzong sent me to warn you: mend your ways at once!"

sentences.zh: 逻卒捕之，下开封狱，一夕方省，则不知向之所为者，乃于狱中尽之。

translations.literal: Patrol soldiers seized him and sent him to Kaifeng prison; only after a night did he come to himself, not knowing what he had done before; he was then executed in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Patrolmen seized him and locked him in Kaifeng jail. Only the next morning did he wake, with no memory of what he had done; he was executed in prison.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年十一月，高宗在扬州，郊祀后数日，有狂人具衣冠，执香炉，携绛囊，拜于行宫门外。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Jianyan, Gaozong was at Yangzhou; several days after the suburban sacrifice, a madman in full dress, holding an incense burner and carrying a crimson pouch, bowed outside the traveling palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Jianyan 2 (1128), with Gaozong at Yangzhou, a few days after the suburban sacrifice a madman in full court dress, incense burner in hand and crimson pouch at his side, prostrated himself outside the mobile palace gate.

sentences.zh: 自言：“天遣我为官家儿。”

translations.literal: He declared of himself: "Heaven sent me to be the Son of the Imperial House."
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed, "Heaven sent me to be the emperor's son."

sentences.zh: 书于囊纸，刻于右臂，皆是语。

translations.literal: He wrote it on the pouch paper and carved it on his right arm—all the same words.
translations.idiomatic: He had written the same words on the pouch and carved them into his right arm.

sentences.zh: 鞫之 不得姓名，高宗以其狂，释不问。

translations.literal: Interrogation could not obtain his name; Gaozong, considering him mad, released him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation failed to learn his name. Gaozong, judging him insane, released him without punishment.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，金人犯维扬。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, the Jurchens attacked Weiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The next second month, Jurchen forces struck Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，有明受之变。

translations.literal: In the third month, there was the Mingshou mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month came the Mingshou coup.

sentences.zh: 绍兴元年四月庚辰，阆州有狂僧衰绖哭于郡谯门曰：“今日佛下世。”

translations.literal: On the gengchen day of the fourth month of the first year of Shaoxing, at Lang Prefecture a mad monk in mourning dress wept at the prefectural watchtower gate, saying: "Today the Buddha descends to the world."
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day of the fourth month in Shaoxing 1 (1131), a frenzied monk in mourning garb wailed at the Lang Prefecture gate: "Today the Buddha descends to the world."

sentences.zh: 且言且哭，实隆祐太后上仙日云。

translations.literal: Weeping as he spoke, it was in fact the day the Empress Dowager Longyou ascended as an immortal.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping as he spoke, he had in fact foretold the day Empress Dowager Longyou would pass away.

sentences.zh: 阆距行都万里，逾月而遗诏至。

translations.literal: Lang was ten thousand li from the mobile capital; more than a month later the death edict arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Lang lay thousands of miles from the temporary capital, yet more than a month later the mourning edict arrived—exactly as he had cried.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十四年正月，绍兴府有狂人突入恩平郡王第，升堂践王坐曰：“我太上皇孙，来赴。”

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year of Chunxi, at Shaoxing Prefecture a madman burst into the mansion of Prince Junping of En, ascended the hall, stepped on the prince's seat, and said: "I am the grandson of the Retired Emperor; I have come to answer the summons."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chunxi 14 (1187), a madman forced his way into Prince Enping's residence in Shaoxing, strode into the hall, sat in the prince's chair, and declared, "I am the Retired Emperor's grandson—I have come in answer to the call."

sentences.zh: 郡鞫讯，终不语，亦狂咎也。

translations.literal: The prefecture interrogated him; in the end he would not speak—this too was a case of mad culprits.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture questioned him, but he never spoke—a madman's omen in the Wood phase.

sentences.zh: 是冬，高宗崩。

translations.literal: That winter, Gaozong died.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Gaozong passed away.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，王薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year, the prince died.
translations.idiomatic: The following eighth month, the prince died as well.

sentences.zh: 绍熙二年十二月庚辰昧爽，成都府有人衰服入帐门，大呼阃帅京镗姓名，亦狂咎也。

translations.literal: At daybreak on the gengchen day of the twelfth month of the second year of Shaoxi, at Chengdu Prefecture someone in mourning dress entered the commander's tent gate and loudly called out the name of the frontier commander Jing Tang—this too was a case of mad culprits.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak on the gengchen day of the twelfth month in Shaoxi 2, a mourner in sackcloth burst through the command tent at Chengdu and shouted the name of frontier commander Jing Tang—another madman's portent.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年十月，蔡州大霖雨，道路行舟。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Jianlong, at Cai Prefecture there was great prolonged rain; boats traveled on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Jianlong 1 (960), torrential rains at Cai Prefecture left the roads navigable by boat.

sentences.zh: 开宝二年八月，帝驻潞州，积雨累日未止。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Kaibao, the emperor was stationed at Lu Prefecture; accumulated rain for many days did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Kaibao 2, the emperor camped at Lu Prefecture while unbroken rains piled up day after day.

sentences.zh: 九月，京师大雨霖。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the capital had great prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the capital was deluged by prolonged rains.

sentences.zh: 五年，京师雨，连旬不止。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, at the capital it rained for more than ten days without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year rain at the capital continued for more than ten days straight.

sentences.zh: 河南、河北诸州皆大霖雨。

translations.literal: All prefectures of Henan and Hebei had great prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: Henan and Hebei prefectures alike suffered torrential rains.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，大霖雨。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year, there was great prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn of the ninth year brought torrential rains.

sentences.zh: 太平兴国二年，道州春夏霖雨不止，平地二丈余。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, at Dao Prefecture spring and summer prolonged rain did not cease; on level ground the water stood more than two zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2, Dao Prefecture saw unending spring and summer rains that left more than twenty feet of standing water on the flats.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，京师连旬雨不止。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year, at the capital rain for more than ten days did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year the capital endured more than ten days of unbroken rain.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，齐州逮捕临邑尉王坦等六人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year, Qi Prefecture arrested the Linyi district defender Wang Tan and five others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year, Qi Prefecture arrested District Defender Wang Tan of Linyi and five companions.

sentences.zh: 系狱未具，一夕，大风雨坏狱户，王坦等 六人并压死。

translations.literal: They were imprisoned before the case was concluded; one night a great wind and rain destroyed the prison gate; Wang Tan and the other six were all crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Held in jail before trial could conclude, they died one night when a violent storm smashed the prison gate and crushed Wang Tan and all six men.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年八月，京师大霖雨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Yongxi, the capital had great prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yongxi 2 the capital was inundated by torrential rain.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年六月，陇城县大雨，坏官私庐舍殆尽，溺死者百三十七人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Chunhua, at Longcheng County great rain destroyed nearly all government and private dwellings; those drowned numbered one hundred thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Chunhua 1 (990), torrential rains at Longcheng County destroyed nearly all public and private buildings and drowned 137 people.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，京师霖雨。

translations.literal: In the third year, the ninth month, the capital had prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year prolonged rains inundated the capital.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，京师大雨，十昼夜不止，朱雀、崇明门外积水尤甚，军营、庐舍多坏。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, the capital had great rain for ten days and nights without stopping; outside the Zhuque and Chongming gates standing water was especially severe, and many military camps and dwellings were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year rain at the capital continued ten days and nights without ceasing; flooding outside the Zhuque and Chongming gates was especially deep, and many barracks and dwellings were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 是秋，陈、颍、宋、亳、许、蔡、徐、濮、澶、博诸州霖雨，秋稼多败。

translations.literal: That autumn, Chen, Ying, Song, Bo, Xu, Cai, Xuzhou, Pu, Chan, and Bo prefectures had prolonged rain, and the autumn crops were largely ruined.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn torrential rains in Chen, Ying, Song, Bo, Xu, Cai, Xuzhou, Pu, Chan, and Bo prefectures ruined much of the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，开封府、宋、亳、陈、颍、泗、寿、邓、蔡、润诸州雨水害稼。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year, Kaifeng Prefecture, Song, Bo, Chen, Ying, Si, Shou, Deng, Cai, and Run prefectures suffered rain damage to the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year rains damaged crops in Kaifeng Prefecture, Song, Bo, Chen, Ying, Si, Shou, Deng, Cai, and Run prefectures.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年五月，昭州大霖雨，害民田，溺死者百五十七人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Xianping, Zhao Prefecture had great prolonged rain, harming the people's fields; those drowned numbered one hundred fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Xianping 1, torrential rains at Zhao Prefecture ruined farmland and drowned 157 people.

sentences.zh: 景德三年八月，青州大雨，坏鼓角楼门，压死者四人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Jingde, Qing Prefecture had great rain; the drum-and-horn tower gate was destroyed; four were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Jingde 3, heavy rains at Qing Prefecture collapsed the drum-and-horn tower gate and killed four people.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年八月，无为军大风雨，折木，坏城门、军营、民舍，压溺千余人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Wuwei Army had great wind and rain; trees were broken; city gates, military camps, and civilian houses were destroyed; more than a thousand were crushed or drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Dazhong Xiangfu 2, a violent storm at Wuwei Army snapped trees, wrecked gates, barracks, and homes, and killed more than a thousand by crushing or drowning.

sentences.zh: 十月，兖州霖雨害稼。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, prolonged rain at Yan Prefecture harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month prolonged rains at Yan Prefecture ruined the harvest.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，升州霖雨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, Sheng Prefecture had prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year Sheng Prefecture suffered prolonged rains.

sentences.zh: 五月辛丑，京师大雨，平地数尺，坏 军营、民舍，多压者，近畿积潦。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day of the fifth month, the capital had great rain; on level ground several chi; military camps and civilian houses were destroyed, many crushed; the near suburbs accumulated floodwater.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the fifth month, rain at the capital stood several feet deep on the flats, wrecked barracks and homes with many crushed beneath, and flooded the capital suburbs.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，建安军大霖雨，害农事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year, Jian'an Army had great prolonged rain, harming agricultural work.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifth year torrential rains at Jian'an Army ruined the farming season.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年七月，京师连雨弥月。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Tianxi, at the capital rain continued for a full month.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tianxi 4 rain at the capital lasted a full month.

sentences.zh: 甲子夜，大雨，流潦泛溢，民舍、军营圮坏大半，多压死者。

translations.literal: On the jiazi night, great rain; overflowing floodwaters; more than half of civilian houses and military camps collapsed; many were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi night torrents overflowed, collapsing more than half the homes and barracks and killing many in the rubble.

sentences.zh: 自是频雨，及冬方止。

translations.literal: From then rain was frequent, and only in winter did it cease.
translations.idiomatic: Rains came again and again until winter finally brought relief.

sentences.zh: 乾兴元年二月，苏、湖、秀州雨，坏民田。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Qianxing, Su, Hu, and Xiu Prefectures had rain that destroyed the people's fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Qianxing 1, rains at Su, Hu, and Xiu prefectures ruined farmland.

sentences.zh: 天圣四年六月戊寅，莫州大雨，坏城壁。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day of the sixth month of the fourth year of Tiansheng, Mo Prefecture had great rain that destroyed the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day of the sixth month in Tiansheng 4, heavy rains at Mo Prefecture breached the city walls.

sentences.zh: 七年，自春涉夏，雨不止。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, from spring through summer, rain did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year rain continued without pause from spring into summer.

sentences.zh: 明道二年六月癸丑，京师雨，坏军营、府库。

translations.literal: On the guichou day of the sixth month of the second year of Mingdao, rain at the capital destroyed military camps and government storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day of the sixth month in Mingdao 2, capital rains wrecked barracks and state storehouses.

sentences.zh: 景祐三年七月庚子，大雨震电。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the seventh month of the third year of Jingyou, great rain with thunder and lightning.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the seventh month in Jingyou 3, torrential rain shook the sky with thunder.

sentences.zh: 庆历，六年七月丁亥，河东大雨，坏忻、代等州城壁。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qingli, on the dinghai day of the seventh month, great rain in Hedong destroyed the city walls of Xin, Dai, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the seventh month in Qingli 6, heavy rains in Hedong breached the walls of Xin, Dai, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 皇祐二年八月，深州大雨，坏民庐舍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Huangyou, Shen Prefecture had great rain that destroyed civilian dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Huangyou 2, heavy rains at Shen Prefecture destroyed civilian homes.

sentences.zh: 四年八月癸未，京城大风雨，民庐摧圮，至有压死者。

translations.literal: On the guiwei day of the eighth month of the fourth year, the capital had great wind and rain; civilian dwellings collapsed, and some were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day of the eighth month in the fourth year, a violent storm in the capital collapsed homes and killed people in the wreckage.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年八月，河北沿边久雨，濒河之民多流移。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Jiayou, along the Hebei frontier rain was prolonged; people along the rivers mostly fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Jiayou 2, prolonged rains along the Hebei frontier drove riverside populations into flight.

sentences.zh: 五月丁未，昼夜大雨。

translations.literal: On the dingwei day of the fifth month, day and night great rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day of the fifth month rain fell day and night.

sentences.zh: 六月乙亥，雨坏太社、太稷坛。

translations.literal: On the yihai day of the sixth month, rain destroyed the altars of the Grand Earth and Grand Grain.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day of the sixth month rains wrecked the altars to Earth and Grain.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，霖雨害稼。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, prolonged rain harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year prolonged rains ruined the harvest.

sentences.zh: 六年七月，河北、京西、淮南、两浙、江南东西淫雨为灾。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year, Hebei, Jingxi, Huainan, the two Zhe circuits, and the eastern and western circuits of Jiangnan all had excessive rain as a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year excessive rains brought disaster to Hebei, Jingxi, Huainan, the two Zhe circuits, and eastern and western Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 闰八月，京师久雨。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month, the capital had prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month the capital endured prolonged rains.

sentences.zh: 是岁频雨，及冬方止。

translations.literal: That year rain was frequent, and only in winter did it cease.
translations.idiomatic: That year rains came repeatedly until winter finally ended them.

sentences.zh: 治平元年，京师自夏历秋，久雨不止，摧真宗及穆、献、懿三后陵台。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiping, at the capital from summer through autumn prolonged rain did not cease, destroying the mausoleum platforms of Zhenzong and the three empresses Mu, Xian, and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiping 1, unbroken summer and autumn rains at the capital collapsed the mausoleum terraces of Zhenzong and Empresses Mu, Xian, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 熙宁元年八月，冀州大雨，坏官私庐舍、城壁。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Xining, Ji Prefecture had great rain that destroyed official and private dwellings and city walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Xining 1, heavy rains at Ji Prefecture wrecked public and private buildings and the city walls.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，陕州大雨，漂溺陕、平陆二县。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year, Shan Prefecture had great rain; Shan and Pinglu counties were washed away and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year floods at Shan Prefecture inundated Shan and Pinglu counties.

sentences.zh: 元丰四年七月，泰州海风驾大雨，漂浸州城，坏公私舍数千楹。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Yuanfeng, at Taizhou a sea wind drove great rain; the prefectural city was washed and inundated; several thousand bays of public and private buildings were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Yuanfeng, a sea gale drove torrential rain at Taizhou, flooding the city and destroying thousands of public and private structures.

sentences.zh: 元祐二年七月丁卯，以雨罢集英殿宴。

translations.literal: On the dingmao day of the seventh month of the second year of Yuanyou, because of rain the feast at Jiying Hall was canceled.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day of the seventh month in Yuanyou 2, rain canceled the banquet at Jiying Hall.

sentences.zh: 元符二年九月，以久雨罢秋宴。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Yuanfu, because of prolonged rain the autumn feast was canceled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Yuanfu 2 prolonged rain canceled the autumn banquet.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，久雨，哲宗大升舆在道陷泥中。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, prolonged rain; Zhezong's great ascent carriage on the road sank into the mud.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year prolonged rains left Zhezong's imperial procession mired in mud on the road.

sentences.zh: 建中靖国元年二月，久雨，时钦圣宪肃皇后、钦慈皇后二陵方用工，诏京西祈晴。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo, prolonged rain; at that time work was underway on the two mausoleums of Empresses Qinsheng Xiansu and Qinci; an edict ordered Jingxi to pray for clear skies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Jianzhong Jingguo 1, prolonged rains hampered construction on the mausoleums of Empresses Qinsheng Xiansu and Qinci, and the court ordered Jingxi to pray for fair weather.

sentences.zh: 崇宁元年七月，久雨，坏京城庐舍，民多压溺而死者。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Chongning, prolonged rain destroyed capital dwellings; many commoners were crushed or drowned to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Chongning 1, prolonged rains collapsed capital buildings and killed many people by crushing or drowning.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，久雨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year rains continued unabated.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，京师久雨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, the capital had prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year the capital endured prolonged rains.

sentences.zh: 又自七月至九月，所在霖雨伤稼，十月始霁。

translations.literal: Again from the seventh month to the ninth month, everywhere prolonged rain harmed the crops; only in the tenth month did it clear.
translations.idiomatic: From the seventh through the ninth month prolonged rains ruined crops everywhere, and skies only cleared in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年四月，京师大雨，天气清寒。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Jingkang, the capital had great rain; the weather was clear and cold.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Jingkang 1, heavy capital rains brought a chill, crystalline cold.

sentences.zh: 又自五月甲申至六月，暴雨伤麦，夏行秋令。

translations.literal: Again from the jiashen day of the fifth month to the sixth month, violent rain harmed the wheat; summer enacted autumn's commands.
translations.idiomatic: From the jiashen day of the fifth month through the sixth month, cloudbursts ruined the wheat crop as summer weather turned autumnal.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年春，淫雨。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Jianyan, excessive rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Jianyan 2 excessive rains fell.

sentences.zh: 三年二月癸亥，高宗初至杭州，久霖雨，占曰：“阴盛，下有阴谋。”

translations.literal: On the guihai day of the second month of the third year, Gaozong had just arrived at Hangzhou; prolonged rain; prognostication says: "Yin is excessive; below there is secret plotting."
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day of the second month in Jianyan 3, soon after Gaozong reached Hangzhou, unending rains fell. The omen books read: "When yin overwhelms yang, conspiracy stirs below."

sentences.zh: 时苗傅、刘正彦为乱。

translations.literal: At that time Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan were in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At that very moment Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan were raising rebellion.

sentences.zh: 五月，霖雨，夏寒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, prolonged rain; summer was cold.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month prolonged rains made summer feel like winter.

sentences.zh: 绍兴元年，行都雨，坏城三百八十丈。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, rain at the mobile capital destroyed three hundred eighty zhang of city wall.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 1 rains at the temporary capital breached 380 zhang of city wall.

sentences.zh: 是岁，婺州雨，坏城。

translations.literal: That year, rain at Wu Prefecture destroyed the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: That same year rains at Wu Prefecture damaged the city walls.

sentences.zh: 三年，雨，自正月朔至于二月。

translations.literal: In the third year, rain from the first day of the first month until the second month.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year rain fell from New Year's Day through the second month.

sentences.zh: 七月，四川霖雨，至于明年正月。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Sichuan had prolonged rain, continuing until the first month of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Sichuan entered prolonged rains that lasted until the first month of the next year.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，淫雨害稼，苏、湖二州为甚。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year, excessive rain harmed the crops; Su and Hu prefectures were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year excessive rains ruined crops, worst in Su and Hu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 九月，久雨，时刘豫连金人入寇；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, prolonged rain; at that time Liu Yu joined the Jurchens in invading;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month prolonged rains fell while Liu Yu allied with the Jurchens to invade;

sentences.zh: 十月，高宗亲征而霁。

translations.literal: in the tenth month, Gaozong personally campaigned and the skies cleared.
translations.idiomatic: in the tenth month Gaozong took the field in person and the weather cleared.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，霖雨，伤蚕麦，行都雨甚。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, prolonged rain harmed silkworms and wheat; rain at the mobile capital was especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year prolonged rains ruined silkworms and wheat, heaviest at the temporary capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，雨，至于明年正月。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, rain continued until the first month of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month rains began and lasted until the first month of the next year.

sentences.zh: 六年五月，久雨不止。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year, prolonged rain did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year unbroken rains continued.

sentences.zh: 七年十月， 高宗如建康，久雨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year, Gaozong went to Jiankang; prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the seventh year, as Gaozong traveled to Jiankang, prolonged rains fell.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，积雨，至于四月，伤蚕麦，害稼。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year, accumulated rain until the fourth month, harming silkworms and wheat and damaging the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year accumulated rains through April ruined silkworms, wheat, and the grain harvest.

sentences.zh: 二十一年夏，襄阳府大雨十余日。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-first year, Xiangyang Prefecture had great rain for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twenty-first year Xiangyang Prefecture saw more than ten days of heavy rain.

sentences.zh: 二十三年六月，大雨，坏军垒、民田。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-third year, great rain destroyed military fortifications and civilian fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-third year heavy rains wrecked fortifications and farmland.

sentences.zh: 三十年五月，久雨，伤蚕 麦，害稼。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirtieth year, prolonged rain harmed silkworms and wheat and damaged the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirtieth year prolonged rains ruined silkworms, wheat, and the grain crop.

sentences.zh: 八月，施州大风雨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Shi Prefecture had great wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month a violent storm struck Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三十二年六月，浙西大霖雨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirty-second year, western Zhe had great prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the thirty-second year western Zhe suffered torrential rains.

sentences.zh: 隆兴元年三月，霖雨，行都坏城三百三十余丈。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Longxing, prolonged rain; at the mobile capital three hundred thirty-odd zhang of city wall were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Longxing 1 prolonged rains at the temporary capital destroyed more than 330 zhang of city wall.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，阴雨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year, overcast rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year gloomy rains persisted.

sentences.zh: 七月，浙西、江东大雨害稼。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, great rain in western Zhe and eastern Jiang harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month heavy rains in western Zhe and eastern Jiang ruined the harvest.

sentences.zh: 八月，风雨逾月。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, wind and rain for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month wind and rain lasted more than a month.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年二月，行都及越、湖、常、润、温、台、明、处九郡寒，败首种，损蚕麦。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Qiandao, the mobile capital and the nine prefectures Yue, Hu, Chang, Run, Wen, Tai, Ming, and Chu were cold; the first planting failed; silkworms and wheat were damaged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Qiandao 1, the temporary capital and nine prefectures—Yue, Hu, Chang, Run, Wen, Tai, Ming, and Chu—suffered cold that ruined the first planting and damaged silkworms and wheat.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，淫雨，至于四月。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, excessive rain until the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year excessive rains continued through the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 夏寒。

translations.literal: Summer was cold.
translations.idiomatic: Summer turned unseasonably cold.

sentences.zh: 江、浙诸郡损稼，蚕麦不登。

translations.literal: Jiang and Zhe prefectures had damaged crops; silkworms and wheat did not mature.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang and Zhe prefectures lost crops; silkworms and wheat failed to ripen.

sentences.zh: 三年五月丙午，泉州大雨，昼夜不止者旬日。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day of the fifth month of the third year, Quan Prefecture had great rain that day and night did not cease for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day of the fifth month in the third year Quan Prefecture endured ten days and nights of unbroken rain.

sentences.zh: 八月，淫雨，江浙淮闽禾、麻、菽、麦、粟多腐。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, excessive rain; in Jiang, Zhe, Huai, and Min the grain, hemp, beans, wheat, and millet mostly rotted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month excessive rains rotted grain, hemp, beans, wheat, and millet across Jiang, Zhe, Huai, and Min.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，阴雨弥月。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, overcast rain for a full month.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year gloomy rains lasted a full month.

sentences.zh: 六年五月，连雨六十余日。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year, continuous rain for more than sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year rain continued for more than sixty days.

sentences.zh: 十一月，连雨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, continuous rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month rains continued unbroken.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，郊祀， 云开于圜丘，百步外有澍雨。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day, suburban sacrifice; clouds parted at the Round Mound; a hundred paces beyond there was timely rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day, during the suburban sacrifice clouds parted over the Round Mound altar while gentle rain fell a hundred paces beyond.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，四川阴雨七十余日。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, Sichuan had overcast rain for more than seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year Sichuan endured more than seventy days of gloomy rain.

sentences.zh: 六月壬寅，大雨彻昼夜，至于己酉。

translations.literal: On the renyin day of the sixth month, great rain through day and night until the jiyou day.
translations.idiomatic: From the renyin day of the sixth month through the jiyou day, rain fell day and night without pause.

sentences.zh: 九年闰正月，淫雨。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month of the ninth year, excessive rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of the ninth year excessive rains fell.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年夏，建康府霖雨，坏城郭。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Chunxi, Jiankang Prefecture had prolonged rain that destroyed the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Chunxi 2 prolonged rains at Jiankang Prefecture damaged the city walls.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，淮、浙积雨损禾麦。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, accumulated rain in Huai and Zhe damaged grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year accumulated rains in Huai and Zhe ruined grain and wheat.

sentences.zh: 八月，浙东西、江东连雨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, eastern and western Zhe and eastern Jiang had continuous rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month eastern and western Zhe and eastern Jiang saw continuous rains.

sentences.zh: 癸未、甲申，行都大风雨。

translations.literal: On the guiwei and jiashen days, the mobile capital had great wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei and jiashen days a violent storm struck the temporary capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，久雨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month prolonged rains continued.

sentences.zh: 十月癸酉，孝宗出手诏决狱，援笔而风起开霁。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day of the tenth month, Xiaozong issued a personal edict to decide cases in prison; as he took up the brush wind arose and the skies cleared.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the tenth month, as Xiaozong personally drafted an edict to review prison cases, wind rose and the skies cleared the moment he lifted his brush.

sentences.zh: 四年九月丁酉、戊戌，绍兴府余姚、上虞二县大风雨。

translations.literal: On the dingyou and wuxu days of the ninth month of the fourth year, Yuyao and Shangyu counties of Shaoxing Prefecture had great wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou and wuxu days of the ninth month in the fourth year violent storms struck Yuyao and Shangyu in Shaoxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年闰六月己亥，阶州暴雨，至于戊申。

translations.literal: On the jihai day of the intercalary sixth month of the fifth year, Jie Prefecture had violent rain until the wushen day.
translations.idiomatic: From the jihai day of the intercalary sixth month through the wushen day in the fifth year, Jie Prefecture endured cloudbursts.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，兴化军、福州福清县暴风雨夜作。

translations.literal: On the yisi day, Xinghua Army and Fuqing County of Fuzhou had violent wind and rain in the night.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day a night storm struck Xinghua Army and Fuqing County in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，衢州霖雨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the fourth month, Quzhou had prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year, Quzhou suffered torrential rains.

sentences.zh: 九月，连雨；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, continuous rain;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month rains continued unbroken;

sentences.zh: 己巳，将郊而霁。

translations.literal: On the jisi day, about to perform the suburban sacrifice, and it cleared.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day, just as the court was to offer the suburban sacrifice, the skies cleared.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，雨腐禾麦。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, rain rotted grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year rains rotted the grain and wheat.

sentences.zh: 五月，久雨，败首种。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, prolonged rain; the first planting failed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month long rains ruined the first planting.

sentences.zh: 十年五月，信州霖雨，自甲戌至于辛巳。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the tenth year, Xin Prefecture had prolonged rain from jiaxu to xinsi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the tenth year torrential rains at Xin Prefecture lasted from the jiaxu day through the xinsi day.

sentences.zh: 八月，福州大霖雨，自己未至于九月乙丑，吉州亦如之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Fuzhou had great prolonged rain from jiwei until the yichou day of the ninth month; Ji Prefecture was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Fuzhou was inundated by torrential rains from the jiwei day until the yichou day of the ninth month, and Ji Prefecture suffered the same.

sentences.zh: 十一年四月，淫雨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eleventh year, excessive rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eleventh year excessive rains fell.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，建康府、太平州大霖雨。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day, Jiankang Prefecture and Taiping Prefecture had great prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day torrential rains struck Jiankang Prefecture and Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六月甲申，处州龙泉县暴雨。

translations.literal: On the jiashen day of the sixth month, Longquan County of Chu Prefecture had a violent downpour.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the sixth month a cloudburst hit Longquan County in Chu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十二年五月、六月，皆霖雨。

translations.literal: In the fifth and sixth months of the twelfth year, both had prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth and sixth months of the twelfth year torrential rains fell throughout.

sentences.zh: 十三年秋，利州路霖，败禾稼穜稑，金、洋、阶、成、岷、凤六州亦如之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the thirteenth year, Lizhou Circuit had rain; grain crops, early rice, and late rice failed; the six prefectures Jin, Yang, Jie, Cheng, Min, and Feng were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn of the thirteenth year rains in Lizhou Circuit ruined grain and both early and late rice, and the six prefectures of Jin, Yang, Jie, Cheng, Min, and Feng fared no better.

sentences.zh: 十五年五月，荆、淮郡国连雨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year, the commanderies and kingdoms of Jing and Huai had continuous rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year the Jing and Huai regions saw unbroken rains.

sentences.zh: 戊午，祁门县霖雨。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day, Qimen County had prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day torrential rains struck Qimen County.

sentences.zh: 十六年四月，西和州霖雨，害禾麦。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year, Xihe Prefecture had prolonged rain, harming grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year prolonged rains at Xihe Prefecture damaged the grain and wheat.

sentences.zh: 五月，浙西、湖北、福建、淮东、利西诸道霖雨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the circuits of western Zhe, Hubei, Fujian, eastern Huai, and western Li all had prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month torrential rains swept the western Zhe, Hubei, Fujian, eastern Huai, and western Lizhou circuits.

sentences.zh: 绍熙元年春，久阴连雨，至于三月。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Shaoxi, long overcast skies and continuous rain lasted until the third month.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Shaoxi 1 gloomy skies and unending rains continued through the third month.

sentences.zh: 夏，阶、成、岷、凤四州霖雨伤麦。

translations.literal: In summer, the four prefectures Jie, Cheng, Min, and Feng had prolonged rain that harmed wheat.
translations.idiomatic: That summer torrential rains in the four prefectures of Jie, Cheng, Min, and Feng ruined the wheat.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，赣州霖雨，连春夏不止，坏城四百九十丈，圮城楼、敌楼凡十五所。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, Gan Prefecture had prolonged rain; from spring through summer it did not cease; four hundred ninety zhang of city wall were destroyed; fifteen gate towers and watchtowers collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year Gan Prefecture entered torrential rains that ran from spring into summer without pause, breaching 490 zhang of city wall and collapsing fifteen gate towers and watchtowers.

sentences.zh: 四月，福建路霖雨，至于五月。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the Fujian Circuit had prolonged rain until the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month prolonged rains along the Fujian Circuit continued into May.

sentences.zh: 七月，利路久雨，伤种麦。
