sentences.zh: 熙宁元年距元丰八年，甘露降凡二十余处。

translations.literal: From the first year of Xining through the eighth year of Yuanfeng, sweet dew descended at more than twenty places in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Xining 1 through the eighth year of Yuanfeng sweet dew was recorded at more than twenty locations.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年距元符三年，亦如之。

translations.literal: From the first year of Yuanyou through the third year of Yuanfu, it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuanyou 1 through Yuanfu 3 the same held true.

sentences.zh: 大观初，甘露降于九成宫帝鼐室。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daguan, sweet dew descended in the Emperor's tripod censer chamber of the Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daguan era sweet dew fell in the imperial censer chamber of the Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，降于尚书省及六曹，御制七言四韵诗赐执政已下。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year it descended at the Department of State Affairs and the Six Ministries; the Emperor composed a seven-character quatrain and bestowed it on the chief administrators and those below.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year it fell at the Department of State Affairs and the Six Ministries; the throne composed a regulated seven-character quatrain and granted it to the chief ministers and their subordinates.

sentences.zh: 其后内自禁中及宣和殿、延福宫、神霄宫，下至三学、开封府、大理寺、宰臣私第，皆有之，岁岁拜表称贺。

translations.literal: Thereafter, within the palace it extended from the Forbidden Precinct and the Xuanhe Hall, Yanfu Palace, and Shenxiao Palace down to the Three Academies, Kaifeng Prefecture, the Court of Judicial Review, and the private residences of chief ministers—all had it; year after year they submitted congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward it appeared throughout the inner quarters—from the Forbidden Precinct, the Xuanhe Hall, Yanfu Palace, and Shenxiao Palace down to the Three Academies, Kaifeng Prefecture, the Court of Judicial Review, and ministers' private homes—and each year officials presented memorials of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，蜀孟昶末年，妇女竞治发为高髻，号“朝天髻”。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong, in the last years of Meng Chang of Shu, women vied to dress their hair in high topknots called "Court-Ascending Buns."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianlong, in the final years of Meng Chang's Shu, women competed to arrange their hair in towering coiffures known as "Court-Ascending Buns."

sentences.zh: 未几，昶入朝京师。

translations.literal: Before long, Chang came to court in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Meng Chang presented himself at court in the capital.

sentences.zh: 江南李煜末年，有卫士秦友登寿昌堂榻，覆其鞋而坐，讯之，风狂不寤。

translations.literal: In the last years of Li Yu of Jiangnan, a guardsman named Qin You climbed onto the couch in the Hall of Longevity and covered his shoes to sit upon them; when questioned, he was deranged and would not wake.
translations.idiomatic: In Li Yu's final years in Jiangnan a guardsman named Qin You mounted the couch in the Hall of Longevity, sat upon his shoes, and when questioned proved mad and could not be roused.

sentences.zh: 识者云：“鞋，履也，李氏将覆于此地而为秦所有乎？

translations.literal: Those who understood omens said: "Shoes are footwear—will the house of Li be overturned in this place and come to belong to Qin?
translations.idiomatic: Those versed in portents said, "A shoe is footwear—will the Li house be overturned here and fall to Qin?

sentences.zh: ‘履’与‘李’、‘友’与‘有’同音，赵与秦，同祖也。”

translations.literal: 'Footwear' and 'Li,' 'You' and 'have' share the same sounds; Zhao and Qin share the same ancestry."
translations.idiomatic: 'Footwear' (lü) and 'Li' are homophones, as are 'You' and 'have' (you); Zhao and Qin sprang from a common ancestry."

sentences.zh: 又煜宫中盛雨水染浅碧为衣，号“天水碧”。

translations.literal: Moreover, within Yu's palace they collected rainwater in abundance and dyed pale blue-green cloth for garments called "Heavenly Water Blue."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at Li Yu's court women gathered rainwater in quantity and dyed garments a pale aquamarine called "Heavenly Water Blue."

sentences.zh: 未几，为王 师所克，士女至京师犹有服之者。

translations.literal: Before long he was overcome by the imperial army; when men and women reached the capital some still wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was conquered by the imperial forces; when Jiangnan's men and women arrived in the capital some still wore that hue.

sentences.zh: 天水，国之姓望也。

translations.literal: Heavenly Water was the surname and eminent clan of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly Water was the dynastic surname and honored lineage of the Tang house.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，京师里巷妇人竞剪黑光纸团靥，又装镂鱼腮中骨，号“鱼媚子”以饰面。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, women in the capital's lanes vied to cut glossy black paper into round cheek ornaments and also to mount and carve the central bone from a fish's gill, calling them "Fish Charms" to adorn the face.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 3 women throughout the capital's neighborhoods competed to cut glossy black paper into round cheek patches and to set carved bones from fish gills—called "Fish Charms"—upon their faces.

sentences.zh: 黑，北方色；

translations.literal: Black is the color of the north;
translations.idiomatic: Black is the color associated with the north;

sentences.zh: 鱼，水族，皆阴类也。

translations.literal: fish belong to the water kind and are all of the yin category.
translations.idiomatic: fish belong to the watery realm and are creatures of yin.

sentences.zh: 面为六阳之首，阴侵于阳，将有水灾。

translations.literal: The face is the foremost of the six yang parts; yin encroaching upon yang foretold a flood disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The face is the chief of the six yang organs; when yin invades yang, floods follow.

sentences.zh: 明年，京师秋冬积雨，衢路水深数尺。

translations.literal: The next year, through autumn and winter the capital saw prolonged rain, and the thoroughfares stood several feet deep in water.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn and winter the capital endured weeks of rain, and the main streets lay several feet under water.

sentences.zh: 景德四年春，京城小儿裂裳为小儿旗，系竿首，相对挥飐，兵斗之象也。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Jingde, children in the capital tore their garments into small banners for children, tied them to the tops of poles, and waved them at one another—an image of soldiers in combat.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Jingde 4 capital children ripped cloth into toy battle flags, fixed them to pole tops, and brandished them at one another—a portent of armed strife.

sentences.zh: 是岁，宜州卒陈进为乱，出师讨平之。

translations.literal: That year the Yizhou soldier Chen Jin rose in rebellion, and troops were dispatched to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Yizhou trooper Chen Jin mutinied, and the court sent an expedition to crush the revolt.

sentences.zh: 绍兴二十一年，行都豪贵竞为小青盖，饰赤油火珠于盖之顶，出都门外，传呼于道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Shaoxing, the great families of the traveling capital vied to use small green canopies and to adorn the tops of the canopies with cinnabar-oil fire pearls, going beyond the city gates with runners calling out along the road.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 21 the wealthy of the mobile capital competed to ride under small green canopies topped with cinnabar-glazed fire pearls, parading beyond the city walls with heralds shouting along the streets.

sentences.zh: 珠者，乘舆服御饰升龙用焉，臣庶以加于小盖，近服妖，亦僭咎也。

translations.literal: Such pearls were used to adorn the ascending dragon on imperial regalia; when commoners and officials added them to small canopies, it approached garment omens and was also a transgression omen.
translations.idiomatic: Those pearls adorned the ascending dragon on imperial equipage; for subjects to fix them on petty canopies smacked of garment omens and usurpation as well.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，士庶家竞以胎鹿皮制妇人冠，山民采捕胎鹿无遗。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, gentry and common households vied to make women's caps from fetal deer hide, and mountain folk hunted fetal deer until none remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year gentle and common families alike raced to fashion women's caps from fetal deerskin, until hill folk had stripped the mountains of unborn fawns.

sentences.zh: 时去宣和未远，妇人服饰犹集翠羽为之，近服妖也。

translations.literal: The time was not far from Xuanhe, and women's dress still gathered kingfisher feathers for ornament—approaching garment omens.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after the Xuanhe era women's attire still relied on kingfisher plumes—another garment omen.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，交阯贡翠羽数百，命焚之通衢，立法以禁。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Jiaozhi presented several hundred kingfisher feathers; an order was given to burn them in the public thoroughfare and to enact statutes forbidding them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Jiaozhi sent several hundred kingfisher plumes as tribute; the court ordered them burned in the open streets and promulgated laws against their use.

sentences.zh: 绍熙元年，里巷妇女以琉璃为首饰。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi, women in the lanes used glass for ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi 1 neighborhood women took to glass jewelry.

sentences.zh: 《唐志》琉璃钗钏有流离之兆，亦服妖也，后连年有流徙之厄。

translations.literal: The Tang Annals state that glass hairpins and bracelets bore the omen of exile and wandering; this too was a garment omen, and in later years there were successive calamities of displacement.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang History notes that glass hairpins and bracelets foretold exile—another garment omen—and for years afterward the realm suffered waves of forced migration.

sentences.zh: 理宗朝，宫妃系前后掩裙而长窣地，名“赶上裙”；

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Lizong, palace consorts tied front-and-back covering skirts that trailed long on the ground, called "Catch-Up Skirts";
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Lizong palace women wore front-and-back overskirts that swept the ground, dubbed "Catch-Up Skirts";

sentences.zh: 梳高髻于顶，曰“不走落”；

translations.literal: they combed high topknots on the crown called "Never Falling";
translations.idiomatic: they piled high coiffures on the crown called "Never Falling Off";

sentences.zh: 束足纤直，名“快上马”；

translations.literal: they bound the feet slender and straight, named "Quick Mount";
translations.idiomatic: they bound their feet slender and straight in a style called "Quick Mount";

sentences.zh: 粉点眼角，名“泪妆”；

translations.literal: they powdered the corners of the eyes, called "Tear Makeup";
translations.idiomatic: they dusted powder at the outer corners of the eyes in "Tear Makeup";

sentences.zh: 剃削童发，必留大钱许于顶左，名“偏顶”，或留之顶前，束以彩缯，宛若博焦之状，或曰“鹁角”。

translations.literal: they shaved children's hair but always left a large coin's breadth on the left of the crown, called "Off-Center Crown," or left it before the crown and bound it with colored silk like the shape of a gambling stake, also called "Pigeon Crest."
translations.idiomatic: they shaved boys' hair yet always left a patch the size of a large coin on the left crown—the "Off-Center Top"—or a forelock bound in colored silk like a gaming counter, also known as "Pigeon Crest."

sentences.zh: 咸淳五年，都人以碾玉为首饰。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianchun, the people of the capital used ground jade for ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianchun 5 the capital's people took to ground jade jewelry.

sentences.zh: 有诗云：“京师禁珠翠，天下尽琉璃。”

translations.literal: A poem runs: "The capital forbids pearl and kingfisher, yet all the realm wears glass.
translations.idiomatic: A contemporary verse ran, "The capital bans pearl and kingfisher, yet all under Heaven is glass."

sentences.zh: 太平兴国三年三月，凿金明池，既掘地，有龟出，殆逾万数。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Taiping Xingguo, when the Jinming Pool was being excavated, as soon as the earth was dug, turtles emerged, nearly numbering more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Taiping Xingguo 3, while the Jinming Pool was being dug, turtles surfaced from the excavated earth in numbers approaching ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年四月，有黑龟甚众，沿汴水而下。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, very many black turtles went downstream along the Bian River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Dazhong Xiangfu 2 a great host of black turtles drifted down the Bian Canal.

sentences.zh: 至和元年二月，信州贡绿毛龟。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Zhihe, Xin Prefecture presented a green-furred turtle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Zhihe 1 Xin Prefecture presented a green-haired turtle as tribute.

sentences.zh: 大观元年闰十月丙戌，都水使者赵霆行河，得两首龟以为瑞，蔡京信之，曰："此齐小白所谓象罔见之而霸者也。"郑居中曰："首岂容有二，而京主之，意殆不可测。"帝命弃龟金明池。

translations.literal: On the bingxu day of the intercalary tenth month of the first year of Daguan, Commissioner of Waterways Zhao Ting inspected the river and obtained two turtle heads, taking them as auspicious omens; Cai Jing believed it and said: "This is what Duke Huan of Qi meant by Xiangwang — upon seeing it one achieves hegemony." Zheng Juzhong said: "How can a head properly have two? Yet Jing upholds it — his intentions are perhaps beyond reckoning." The emperor ordered the turtles discarded in Jinming Pool.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day of the intercalary tenth month of Daguan 1 (1107), Commissioner of Waterways Zhao Ting inspected the riverbed and found two turtle heads, which were hailed as omens; Cai Jing accepted them and said, "This is what Duke Huan of Qi meant by Xiangwang—seeing it brings hegemony." Zheng Juzhong said, "How can a head properly have two? Yet Jing upholds it—his intentions are perhaps beyond reckoning." The emperor ordered the turtles discarded in Jinming Pool.

sentences.zh: 政和四年，瑞州进六目龟。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenghe, Rui Prefecture presented a six-eyed turtle.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 4 Rui Prefecture sent up a six-eyed turtle.

sentences.zh: 五年，博州进白龟。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Bo Prefecture presented a white turtle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Bo Prefecture presented a white turtle.

sentences.zh: 绍兴八年五月，汴京太康县大雷雨，下冰龟数十里，随大小皆龟形，具首足卦 文。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Shaoxing, a great thunderstorm at Taikang County in Bianjing brought down ice turtles for several tens of li; large and small alike were in the form of turtles, complete with head, feet, and hexagram markings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Shaoxing 8 a violent thunderstorm at Taikang County near Bianjing rained ice turtles across dozens of li; each piece, great or small, took a turtle's shape with head, feet, and hexagram patterns upon them.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年，舒州民献龟，骈生二首，不能伸缩。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiandao, a commoner of Shuzhou presented a turtle with twin heads born side by side, unable to retract or extend.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 5 a man of Shuzhou offered up a turtle born with two heads joined, neither able to withdraw into its shell.

sentences.zh: 郡守张栋纵之灊山，近龟孽也。

translations.literal: The prefect Zhang Dong released it on Qian Mountain; this was a turtle calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Dong released it on Mount Qian—a clear turtle portent.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十四年春，楚州境上龟大小死者蔽野。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourteenth year of Jiading, within Chu Prefecture dead turtles large and small covered the fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Jiading 14 dead turtles of every size carpeted the countryside within Chu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年八月，黄州群鸡夜鸣，至冬不止。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Xianping, at Huang Prefecture flocks of chickens crowed at night until winter without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Xianping 3 chickens at Huang Prefecture crowed through the night, and the clamor did not stop until winter.

sentences.zh: 绍兴初，陈州民家鸡忽人言，近鸡祸也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxing, at a commoner's home in Chen Prefecture a chicken suddenly spoke in human words; this was a chicken portent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxing era household chicken in Chen Prefecture suddenly spoke like a person—a cock omen of ill.

sentences.zh: 松阳县民家鸡生三足，县治有鸡伏卵， 毛生壳外，近鸡祸，亦毛孽也。

translations.literal: At a commoner's home in Songyang County a chicken was born with three legs; at the county seat a hen brooded eggs with hair growing outside the shell; this was a chicken portent and also a hair calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In Songyang County a chicken hatched with three legs, and at the yamen a brooding hen produced eggs with feathers sprouting outside the shell—both a cock portent and a hair anomaly.

sentences.zh: 乾道六年，西安县官塘有物，鸡首人身，高丈余，昼见于野。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiandao, at the official pond in Xi'an County there was a creature with a chicken's head and human body, more than a zhang tall, seen by day in the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 6 a creature with a cock's head and human body, standing more than ten feet tall, appeared by day at the official pond in Xi'an County.

sentences.zh: 庆元三年，饶州军营鸡卵出蛇，近鸡孽，亦蛇孽也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingyuan, at a Raozhou military camp a chicken egg produced a snake; this was a chicken calamity and also a snake calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingyuan 3 a snake hatched from a chicken egg at a Raozhou barracks—an omen of both cock and serpent.

sentences.zh: 婺源县张村民家雌鸡化为雄，烹之，形冠距而腹卵孕。

translations.literal: At Zhang Village in Wuyuan County a household hen transformed into a rooster; when cooked it had comb and spurs in form yet the belly held developing eggs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhang Village, Wuyuan County, a hen turned into a rooster; cooked, it bore comb and spurs yet its belly still held eggs in development.

sentences.zh: 同里洪氏家雄鸡伏子，中一雏三足。

translations.literal: In the same village the Hong household had a rooster brooding chicks; among them one chick had three legs.
translations.idiomatic: In the same hamlet the Hong family's rooster hatched a brood in which one chick had three legs.

sentences.zh: 咸淳五年，常州鸡羽生距。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianchun, at Chang Prefecture chickens' feathers grew spurs.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianchun 5 chickens at Chang Prefecture sprouted spurs from their feathers.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年夏，相、金、均、房、商五州鼠食苗。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Jianlong, Xiang, Jin, Jun, Fang, and Shang prefectures had rats eating the seedlings.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Jianlong 1 rats devoured seedlings in Xiang, Jin, Jun, Fang, and Shang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，商州鼠食苗。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year, Shang Prefecture had rats eating seedlings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year rats ate the seedlings at Shang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年九月，金州鼠食苗。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Qiande, Jin Prefecture had rats eating seedlings.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Qiande 5 rats devoured seedlings at Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太平兴国七年十月，岳州鼠害稼。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo, Yue Prefecture had rats harming the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Taiping Xingguo 7 rats ruined the harvest at Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 绍兴十六年，清远、翁源、真阳三县鼠食稼，千万为群。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shaoxing, Qingyuan, Wengyuan, and Zhenyang counties had rats eating crops in groups of tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 16 rats in tens of millions devoured crops in Qingyuan, Wengyuan, and Zhenyang counties.

sentences.zh: 时广东久旱，凡羽鳞皆化为鼠。

translations.literal: At that time Guangdong had long drought; all creatures with feathers and scales turned into rats.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had suffered a long drought, and every feathered or scaled creature was said to have turned into a rat.

sentences.zh: 有获鼠于田者，腹犹蛇文，渔者夜设纲，旦视皆鼠。

translations.literal: Some caught rats in the fields whose bellies still bore snake markings; fishermen set nets at night and at dawn found only rats.
translations.idiomatic: Rats taken in the fields still bore snake patterns on their bellies; fishermen who set nets at night found only rats in them at dawn.

sentences.zh: 自夏徂秋，为患数月方息，岁为饥，近鼠妖也。

translations.literal: From summer through autumn the plague lasted several months before subsiding; that year brought famine; this was a rat portent.
translations.idiomatic: From summer through autumn the scourge lasted months before easing, and famine followed—a rat anomaly in the Wood phase.

sentences.zh: 乾道九年，隆兴府鼠千万为群，害稼。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qiandao, at Longxing Prefecture rats formed groups of tens of millions and harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 9 rats at Longxing Prefecture gathered in millions and ruined the harvest.

sentences.zh: 淳熙五年八月，淮东通、泰、楚、高邮黑鼠食禾既，岁大饥。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year of Chunxi, in eastern Huai at Tong, Tai, Chu, and Gaoyou black rats finished eating the grain; that year brought great famine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Chunxi 5 black rats in eastern Huai at Tong, Tai, Chu, and Gaoyou stripped the grain fields bare, and famine followed.

sentences.zh: 时江陵府郭外，群鼠多至塞路，其色黑、白、青、黄各异，为车马践死者不可胜计，逾三月乃息。

translations.literal: At that time outside Jiangling Prefecture city rats in such numbers blocked the roads; their colors black, white, green, and yellow differed; those trampled by carts and horses were beyond counting; only after more than three months did it cease.
translations.idiomatic: Outside Jiangling city rats clogged the roads in black, white, green, and yellow hordes; countless were crushed under wheels and hooves, and the plague did not abate for more than three months.

sentences.zh: 绍熙四年，饶州民家二小鼠食牛角，三徙牛牢不免，角穿肉瘠以毙，近鼠妖也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxi, at a commoner's home in Raozhou two small rats ate an ox's horn; though the ox was moved three times to different pens it could not escape; the horn pierced the flesh and the ox wasted away and died; this was a rat portent.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi 4 two tiny rats at a Raozhou farmhouse gnawed an ox's horn; though the beast was moved three times between pens they could not be stopped—the horn bored into the flesh until the ox wasted away and died, a rat portent.

sentences.zh: 庆元元年六月，番阳县民家一猫带数十鼠，行止食息皆同，如母子相哺者，民杀猫而鼠舐其血。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Qingyuan, at a commoner's home in Poyang County one cat led several dozen rats; in going, stopping, eating, and resting they were all alike, as if mother and young nursed each other; the people killed the cat and the rats licked its blood.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Qingyuan 1 a cat at a Poyang County home led dozens of rats that moved, fed, and rested in perfect unison like a nursing family; when the people killed the cat, the rats licked its blood.

sentences.zh: 鼠象盗，猫职捕，而反相与同处，司盗废职之象也，与唐龙朔洛州猫鼠同占。

translations.literal: The rat symbolizes theft; the cat's duty is to catch; yet they instead dwelt together—an image of those who oversee theft abandoning their office; the same prognostication as cats and rats together at Luozhou in Longshuo of the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Rats stand for thieves and cats for their hunters, yet here predator and prey lived as allies—an omen that those charged to suppress crime had abandoned their post, matching the Tang omen of cats and rats together at Luozhou in Longshuo.

sentences.zh: 绍兴三年八月辛亥，尚书省后楼无故自坏。

translations.literal: On the xinhai day of the eighth month of the third year of Shaoxing, the rear building of the Secretariat collapsed for no reason.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day of the eighth month in Shaoxing 3 the rear hall of the Secretariat collapsed without apparent cause.

sentences.zh: 庆元元年夏，建昌军民居木柱有声如牛鸣者，三日乃止。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Qingyuan, at Jianchang Army in civilian dwellings wooden pillars made sounds like oxen lowing; after three days it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Qingyuan 1 wooden pillars in homes at Jianchang Army lowed like cattle for three days before falling silent.

sentences.zh: 咸淳九年，丞相贾似道起复之日，在越上私第，方拜家庙，忽闻内有裂帛声，众宾愕然，密询左右，知家庙栋裂，皆逡巡而退。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianchun, on the day Chancellor Jia Sidao resumed office, at his private residence in Yue, just as he was worshipping at the family temple, suddenly from within came the sound of tearing silk; all the guests were startled; secretly inquiring of attendants they learned the family temple beams had split; all withdrew hesitantly.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianchun 9, on the day Chancellor Jia Sidao returned to office, he was offering at his family shrine in his Yue residence when a sound like ripping silk came from within. The guests froze; whispered inquiries revealed the shrine beams had split, and one by one they slipped away.
